hero.title: Drop the footage. Get the timeline.
hero.lead: TakeSync lines up every camera, recorder and lav mic by their sound — no timecode, no slate, no clapping. Then hands the synced timeline to Premiere Pro.
hero.fine: Version 1.0 for Macs with Apple Silicon. 7 days free, works offline.
pain.title: A wedding is hundreds of files from every device you brought.
pain.text: Cameras, a drone, a phone, a recorder on the DJ desk, lav mics on the groom, the officiant and the parents. Lining that up by hand eats the first evening of every edit. TakeSync does it while you make coffee.
feat.title: What it does for you
feat.1: Every clip is matched to the others by its audio. Any camera, phone, recorder or lav works — no timecode or slate needed.
feat.2: B-roll from a camera rolling on its own has no sound partner. TakeSync places it by the camera’s clock, at the time of day it was shot.
feat.3: A song played twice or an interview over the ceremony can look like a match. Every match is checked against the device clocks, and the ones that can’t be true are dropped.
feat.4: The timeline follows the real time of day: ceremony, portraits, speeches, first dance. Long stretches where nobody recorded are squeezed out.
feat.5: One tick adds a second sequence where camera audio is replaced by the recorder or lav. Overlapping clips get their own tracks, so nothing hides under anything.
feat.6: Your footage never leaves your Mac. No upload, no account, no internet needed to sync.
feat.7: TakeSync checks whether your footage sits on an SSD, a spinning hard drive or a network share, and reads each the fastest way: every core on an SSD, two files at a time from an HDD, several drives at once. Footage it has already analysed is never decoded again.
feat.8: Three steps, one Sync button, nothing to configure. Analysis runs in the background, so the window stays responsive while TakeSync works.
how.title: Three steps
how.s1: Each camera, recorder or mic folder becomes a track. Proxies are detected — keep them or skip them.
mock.drop: Drop camera and recorder folders here
how.s2: TakeSync listens to every clip, finds where they overlap and builds the timeline — by sound first, by clock for the rest.
how.s3: The TakeSync panel inside Premiere shows every export. One click imports the synced sequence into your open project, reusing the media you already have — no duplicates.

faq.title: Questions
faq.q1: Do I need timecode or a slate?
faq.a1: No. TakeSync compares the sound recorded by different devices at the same time. Cameras without timecode and phones work fine.
faq.a2: MP4, MOV, WAV, AIFF, M4A and MP3 out of the box. MXF, MTS and other formats work after you install FFmpeg from Settings.
faq.q3: What happens to a clip with no sound partner?
faq.a3: If its camera’s clock is reliable, the clip goes on the timeline at the time it was recorded and is marked so you can check it. Otherwise it’s marked as not synced, and on export you can move such clips to the end.
faq.q4: Does it fix drift on long recordings?
faq.a4: Yes. TakeSync detects when a recorder runs slightly fast or slow against the cameras and corrects the audio.
faq.q5: What about Final Cut Pro, DaVinci Resolve and Windows?
faq.a5: Final Cut Pro and DaVinci Resolve export is being tested now. Windows is in development. They arrive as free updates.
faq.q6: Monthly, yearly or lifetime — what’s the difference?
faq.a6: Only how you pay. A subscription keeps TakeSync working while it’s active, and you can cancel any time. The lifetime licence is paid once and never expires. Every plan includes all features and updates.
